IN T HE COU RT OF MS. SARWAT REHMAN , LEARNED CIVIL JUDGE, RAWALPINDI 
 
 Civil Suit No. ________ / 20 24 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Zakir Hussain 
 
 v ersus 
 
 M/s. Mall 35 etc 
 
 ( SUIT FOR SPECIFIC PERFORMANCE OF AGREEMENT TO SELL No. 574 DATED 29 SEP 2020, POSSESSION, MENSE PROFIT, COMPENSATION FOR BREACH OF AGREEMENT, DAMAGES, MANDATORY AND PERPETUAL INJUNCTION) 
 
 Application under Order IX Rule 7 read with section 151 Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 for setting aside Order dated 2 4 . 1 0.202 4 initiating ex-parte proceedings agains t the Applicant/Defendant No.1 . 
 
 Respectfully sheweth ; 
 That the titled sui t is pending adjudication before this learned Court, and is fixed for hearing today i.e. , 11-12 - 2024 . 
 T he titled application is being filed by Mall 35, a partnership Firm registered under the laws of Pakistan (hereinafter referred to as the Applicant Firm / Defendant No. 1 ) and , therefore , the Applicant Firm /Defendant No. 1 is filing the instant Application through Syed Hasan Ali Shah, who is fully conversant with the facts of the case and has been duly authorized to file, sign and verify the pleadings in order to defend against titled Suit 
 
 ORDERS PASSED BY THE LEARNED COURT 
 That the learned Court passed the following Orders which subsequently lead to the ex parte proceedings: 
 Order dated 19 - 07 - 2024 
 T he titled suit was filed on 1 9-07 -2024 and the learned Judge was pleased to Order that the Summons be sent to the Defenda nts “ through registered envelope AD , courier service, modern device … ” and the case was adjourned t o 29 - 0 7 - 202 4 . 
 
 Order dated 29 - 0 7 - 202 4 
 On 2 9-07 -2024 honourable judges were transferred and suit was adjourned to 03 - 1 0-2024. 
 
 Order dated 03 - 10 -2024 
 On 03 - 10 -2024 the Honourable Court Order that the Defendants be Summoned “ through press publication in the newspaper daily “Jang” … ” and the case was adjourned t o 24 - 10 - 202 4 . 
 
 Order dated 24-10 -2024 
 On 24 - 1 0-2024 ordered that ‘ Despite publication no one appeared on behalf of Defendants since morning. Now time is to be over. Therefore, Defendants are hereby proceeded against ex-parte’ 
 
 The Applicant came to know of pendency of the titled suit on 28-11-2024 when Applicant’s counsel visited the Court premises to attend another case titled “Nadia Gulnaz vs V4 Capital” . After obtaining copies of case file, instant application is being filed which is well within time 
 
 That through the instant Application, the Applicant s seeks setting aside of ex-parte Order dated 2 4 . 1 0.202 4 , as passed by th e learned Judge , and the consequent ex-parte proceedings, inter alia , on the following : 
 G R O U N D S 
 That the Applicant has never been served through all the necessary modes of service in accordance with law, more specifically, the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (“ CPC ”). This fact is evident from the record of this learned Court. Therefore, the Ex-Parte Order is liable to be set-aside. 
 
 That there is nothing on record to show that the Applicant had knowledge of the pending proceedings or the respective dates of hearings and consequently was avoiding service. That the record of the case is also silent in terms of any acknowledgement of the receipt of the registered communication or an endorsement by a courier messenger or postal employee that the Applicant refused to take delivery of summons, as envisaged in Order V Rule 10A, CPC . In fact, there is no record of any signature of any of Applicant ’s employees acknowledging the delivery of the said notices. Since the notices were never received by the Applicant , hence, it never got duly informed of filing of the titled suit . Therefore, the e x- p arte Order is liable to be set-aside/recalled on this score also. 
 
 That without prejudice to the averments made herein above, it may kindly be noted that the Plaintiff has failed to attach any evidence pertaining to the delivery of the TCS courier sent to the Applicant’s correct /actual address, as mentioned in the contracts/agreements signed by the plaintiff himself, nor any acknowledgment of such courier is available on the record. Therefore, Ex-Parte Order is liable to be set aside on this account also. 
 
 That only one mode of service was adopted before ex parte proceedings commenced against the Applicant . Under such circumstances, the learned Court could not have satisfied itself or ensured that the Applicant was avoiding service or had knowledge of the pending proceedings without first availing all modes of service that the Court has the authority to use under Order V, CPC. Hen ce, it is clear that the summon was not properly served on the Applicant , therefore , the Ex-Parte Order is liable to be set-aside/recalled. 
 That , apparently the process server of this learned Court never went to the actual address for the service of summon issued by this learned Court. Hence the Ex-Parte Order is liable to be set-aside. 
 That this learned Court while passing the Ex-Parte Order against the Applicant did not consider the fact that summons/notices were neither witnessed by any person from the locality nor was any affidavit given in support of report therein. Therefore, the Ex-Parte Order had been passed by this learned Court in contravention of mandatory provisions of law, which is not sustainable in the eye of law. 
 That it is trite law that suits should be properly adjudicat ed on merits instead of being knocked out on the basis of technicalities; therefore, given the fact that valuable legal rights of the Applicant are involved in the matter, it will be in the interest of justice that the ex-parte proceedings initiated through Order dated 2 4 - 1 0 - 202 4 b e set-aside and the Applicant be given a fair opportunity of hearing and be allowed to defend itself in the titled suit . 
 That the stance of the Plaintiff , as stated in the plaint , is unfounded and the submissions of the Applicant or its respective stance before this learned Court through Written Statement and evidence in support there of, as well as the opportunity to challenge the version of the Plaintiff by subjecting the same to cross examination, are essential for fair and proper adjudication of the suit . 
 That even otherwise, it is the settled dictum of the Superior Courts of Pakistan that in the absence of any clear provisions in the CPC prohibiting the appearance and taking part in the proceedings by the defendant, there is no legal bar in allowing the defendant to defend its rights. It has been held in umpteen judicial precedents that the rules of procedure i.e. CPC, are meant to advance justice and preserve the rights of litigants and they are not to be interpreted in a way as to hamper the administration of justice. Hence, it is the right of the Applicant to take part in proceedings which have been proceeded ex-parte against it. 
 That from the averment s made herein a bove , it transpire s that ex-parte Order dated 24 . 1 0.202 4 has been passed in a mechanical and hasty manner as mandatory requirements to effect service upon the Applicant have not been fulfilled and the Applicant has been deprived of it s lawful and legitimate right of defence . Hence, the said Ex-part e Order is liable to be set-aside /re-called. 
 That even otherwise, the right of fair trial is a fundamental right of every person, violation of which will lead to one inescapable conclusion, i.e. , destruction of the justice system. It is most respectfully submitted that any further proceedings in the instant matter shall be a direct violation of the said fundamental right of fair trial. Therefore, the Ex-Parte Order is liable to be set aside. 
 That it is trite law that no one should be condemned unheard. In the titled suit the golden principle of justice Audi alteram partem has severely compromised rendering the judicial process unsustainable. The Applicant has a valid undeniable right of being heard and treated as per law. 
 That the Applicant very respectfully seeks leave to raise addition al grounds at the bar. 
 PRAYER: 
 In the circumstances, it is respectfully prayed that the instant Application may kindly be accepted, and ex-parte Order dated 2 4 . 1 0 . 202 4 be set aside, as earlier passed by th is learned C ourt, and the Applicant may be allowed to join the proceedings in the titled suit and subsequent ex-parte proceedings conducted in the titled suit may graciously be set aside . 
 Any other relief which this learned Court may deem fit in favour of the Applicant may also graciously be awarded.
